title: GET /users, GET /users/{id} and DELETE /users/{id} return every user's password in plain text
description: Anyone on the internet, without logging in, can open the user list and read every customer's password in plain text - and those passwords really work to log in. Passwords should never be sent back by the system. With them, a stranger can take over any customer account.
preconditions: None - no token or login needed
steps: Send GET https://fakestoreapi.com/users with no Authorization header
Every user object contains 'password' in plain text (all 10 users)
GET /users/1 and DELETE /users/1 also return the password
POST /auth/login with any leaked username + password returns a token (verified for 3 users)
expected: User responses never contain passwords (plain or hashed); user data requires authentication.
actual: 200 OK without any token; 'password' returned in plain text for every user, and the passwords are valid for login.
notes: The OpenAPI User schema itself lists 'password' as a response field - the spec should be fixed too.
